short_description: Nightly ETL job fails at audit step — wbbaudit program not found
description: The nightly WBBAW ETL job completed the load step successfully but failed immediately at the audit step. Job runner log shows: 'ERROR: program wbbaudit not found at expected path /opt/wbbaw/bin/wbbaudit'. Extract and load completed with RC_OK. Audit failure triggered on_failure routing to notify_failure step. On-call paged at 02:17 UTC. Downstream job wbb-reporting-refresh was not triggered. Morning reports unavailable at 06:00 UTC.
work_notes: L3 investigation confirmed no wbbaudit.py exists in the ETL codebase or deployment artifact. Reviewed user story export — WBB-AW-014 (implement post-load audit step) was recorded as IN PROGRESS at time of last artifact export; it was never completed or deployed. Job_config.yaml references the program under step name 'audit' with COMPARE_COUNTS=true and ALERT_ON_VARIANCE=5. The program does not exist. Workaround applied: commented out audit step in job_config.yaml in production, routing load step on_success directly to notify_success. Change ticket CHG-WBB-0029 raised.
resolution_notes: Workaround active: audit step bypassed via CHG-WBB-0029. Load routes directly to notify_success. ALERT_ON_VARIANCE and COMPARE_COUNTS parameters are not enforced. DEF-WBB-0041 raised to implement wbbaudit. Morning reports recovered by 07:30 UTC via manual trigger of wbb-reporting-refresh.

short_description: Weekly onboarding volume shows counts by submission date not approval date — incorrect per BRD
description: The Operations team raised a discrepancy between the weekly onboarding volume dashboard and the approval activity reported by the WBB operational platform. Dashboard shows 342 approvals in the week of 2026-02-09; operational platform shows 289. On investigation the difference is because the warehouse vw_weekly_onboarding_volume view counts applications by submission date (submitted_date_key), not approval date (approved_date_key). BRD §5 specifies that volume metrics must reflect the date the decision was made, not the date of submission. Applications submitted one week but approved the next inflate the submission-week count and deflate the approval-week count.
work_notes: L3 confirmed this is a known as-built deviation documented in target_schema.sql fact_application comment: 'submitted_date_key is the primary date dimension used for weekly volume reporting. The BRD §5 specifies that volume metrics should be counted by the date the application was approved... approved_dt was not available in the source schema at the time the ETL was built.' The approved_date_key column is populated on fact_application where approved_dt is available. The reporting view has not been updated. Communicated to Operations that the deviation is documented and in the backlog.
resolution_notes: Incident closed as Known Gap — documented deviation from BRD §5. Operations team acknowledges and has accepted submission-date reporting as interim behaviour. Backlog item to update vw_weekly_onboarding_volume to join on approved_date_key recorded as WBB-AW-020. No ETL change required; view definition change only.

short_description: Top decline reasons report returns NULL for all decline_description values
description: The Finance team is trying to run the BRD §6 report: 'Top decline reasons. Among declined applications, what are the most common reasons, ranked?' All attempts to query fact_application for a human-readable decline reason return NULL or column-not-found errors. The fact_application table has no decline_description column. The staging JSONL file does contain the decline_description field (confirmed by L3 by inspecting a sample staging file). The column was never loaded into the warehouse.
work_notes:
L3 data flow trace:
1. wbbxtr.py EXTRACT_QUERY performs LEFT JOIN to decline_reason table and aliases reason_description as decline_description. Field is present in staging JSONL. CONFIRMED.
2. wbbldr.py load_fact function reads staged records but decline_description is absent from the INSERT tuple and column list. CONFIRMED — field is silently dropped.
3. target_schema.sql fact_application DDL has no decline_description column. fact_application header comment explicitly states: 'Note: there is no decline_description column on this fact.'
4. User story WBB-AW-011 is marked Done with acceptance criterion '[x] fact_application carries a human-readable decline reason for declined applications' checked by P. Nguyen on 2026-01-16. Story closure verified only that staging file contained the field, not that it reached the warehouse.
Escalated to DEV as DEF-WBB-0048. BRD §6 report is currently undeliverable against the current warehouse schema.

short_description: Query using business_segment column name returns 'column not found' on dim_customer
description: A new analyst ran a query against wbbaw.dim_customer using the column name business_segment as described in BRD §3 and received a column-not-found error. The column does not exist under that name in the warehouse. The analyst then tried business_category (the source schema name from source_schema.sql) and also received an error. The correct warehouse column name is segment.
work_notes:
L3 confirmed the three-name discrepancy documented in the spec:
- BRD §3 uses business_segment
- Source schema (wbb.customer) uses business_category
- Warehouse (wbbaw.dim_customer) uses segment (conformed naming convention)
The ETL maps source business_category to warehouse segment at load time (wbbldr.py upsert_dim_customer comment). The BRD has not been updated. Analyst guidance provided: use segment for warehouse queries.
resolution_notes: Incident closed. Knowledge gap confirmed in spec §6 D2. Analyst guidance: warehouse column is segment; BRD and source use different names for the same concept. Added to FAQ. Flagged for BRD update in WBB-AW-021.

short_description: COMMIT_INTERVAL=5000 config parameter does not appear to batch warehouse commits
description: Operations asked whether the load step was committing in batches of 5000 as specified by COMMIT_INTERVAL=5000 in job_config.yaml. Reviewing the wbbldr.py source, the load issues a single commit after all dimension and fact rows are processed. There is no batched-commit loop in the code. For a typical nightly load of 8000-12000 rows, all rows are written and committed in a single transaction.
work_notes: L3 confirmed: COMMIT_INTERVAL is specified in job_config.yaml load step params but is not read or used anywhere in wbbldr.py. The current load issues one commit at the end. This is an open question documented in spec §7 Q5. The parameter was likely intended for a batched implementation that was not built. Under normal load volumes this is not a problem. If load volumes increase significantly, a single large transaction could become a risk.
resolution_notes: Closed as Known Gap / documented open question (spec §7 Q5). No current impact at present data volumes. If load grows beyond ~50,000 rows per night, revisit batched commit implementation. DEF-WBB-0051 raised as a backlog item.

short_description: dim_customer.first_product_type column is NULL for all customers
description: A data analyst noticed that the first_product_type column on wbbaw.dim_customer is NULL for every customer row in the warehouse. Expected: the column should show the product type of the first banking product activated for each customer. The column was added to the dim_customer DDL on 2026-01-20 per the schema comment.
work_notes: L3 confirmed: wbbldr.py upsert_dim_customer explicitly sets first_product_type to NULL for all upserts with comment 'first_product_type: populated by a separate job'. The nightly ETL does not populate this column. The separate job referenced in the comment has not been identified in the available codebase. There is no wbb-product-refresh job visible in the job_config.yaml.
resolution_notes: Closed as Known Gap — spec §7 Q9 documents that first_product_type population is deferred to 'a separate job' not yet implemented. Column will remain NULL until that job is built and deployed. Analyst noted for reporting purposes.

short_description: Slack channel #wbb-data-ops not receiving ETL job success or failure alerts
description: The #wbb-data-ops Slack channel has received no ETL alerts since 2026-02-03. Operations team thought the channel was misconfigured. On investigation, the issue is that the audit step workaround (CHG-WBB-0029 — routing load directly to notify_success) bypasses the wbbnotify program, and the wbbnotify program itself is not present in the deployment.
work_notes: L3 confirmed: no wbbnotify.py file exists in the ETL codebase (same class of issue as wbbaudit — program referenced in job_config.yaml but never implemented). The workaround applied in CHG-WBB-0029 routes load success directly to notify_success step, which calls wbbnotify. Since wbbnotify does not exist, the step fails silently (job runner was configured to ignore terminal step failures). Failure alerts were also not reaching the channel. Spec §7 Q8 documents wbbnotify as unimplemented.
resolution_notes: Incident closed. Root cause: wbbnotify not implemented — same gap category as wbbaudit (spec §5.6, §5.7, Q8). Interim workaround: Operations team monitoring job runner dashboard manually pending wbbnotify implementation. DEF-WBB-0055 raised. Related to DEF-WBB-0041 (wbbaudit) — both missing programs should be implemented together.

short_description: Nightly load fails with foreign-key violations on fact_application after 2026-04-28 platform refresh
description: Starting with the run of 2026-04-29 (01:00 UTC), the nightly load step began aborting with PostgreSQL foreign-key violations: 'insert or update on table "fact_application" violates foreign key constraint "fact_application_customer_key_fkey" — Key (customer_key)=(...) is not present in table "dim_customer"'. On-call paged at 02:40 UTC. The failures affect applications from RETURNING customers (customers already present in dim_customer from earlier runs); applications from brand-new customers load without error. Extract completed normally and the staging file was well-formed. The only change in the preceding 24 hours was the 2026-04-28 platform refresh (CHG-WBB-0058) — no application code was deployed.
work_notes:
L3 root-cause trace:
1. Correlated onset (2026-04-29 run) with runtime_environment.md deployment history: 2026-04-28 platform refresh CHG-WBB-0058 upgraded the base image (Python 3.10.13 -> 3.12.3, psycopg2-binary 2.9.5 -> 2.9.9, Debian 11 -> 12). No ETL code change.
2. wbbldr.py generates surrogate keys in application code: customer_key = abs(hash(('cust', customer_id))) & ((1<<63)-1). The hash input is a tuple containing the string 'cust', so CPython salts the hash per-process via PYTHONHASHSEED.
3. runtime_environment.md §3: the legacy bullseye base image set PYTHONHASHSEED=0 (fixed seed -> stable string hashes across process restarts). The standardised 2026.04 image does not carry that override -> PYTHONHASHSEED is now unset -> a fresh random salt every job run.
4. Effect: customer_key for a given customer_id now differs from the value computed under the old runtime. upsert_dim_customer uses ON CONFLICT (customer_id) DO UPDATE SET ... which does NOT update customer_key, so existing dim_customer rows retain their OLD key; load_fact writes the NEW key onto fact_application. The fact FK (customer_key -> dim_customer.customer_key) no longer resolves for returning customers. New customers are inserted into dim_customer with the new key in the same run, so their facts resolve.
5. This is the exact risk recorded as unassessed in Spec §4.4 / §7 Q4 ('not guaranteed to be stable across Python version upgrades or platform changes').
Interim mitigation applied 2026-04-29: re-pinned PYTHONHASHSEED=0 in the wbbaw-batch job environment and ran ETL_MODE=FULL to rebuild dim/fact keys consistently. Nightly loads green again from 2026-04-30. This restores the OLD seed; it does not fix the underlying dependence on a salted hash. Escalated to DEV as DEF-WBB-0060.
